new_statements.quote: Usually, the second-to-last syllable is stressed in the Owa language, e.g., auragi /ɐʊ.ˈɾɐ.gɪ/ 'married'. But occasionally the antepenultimate (third-to-last) syllable is stressed, as in fefene /ˈfɛ.fɛ.nɛ/ 'female'. However, stress placement depends on the context, specifically where it is located in the sentence; therefore, it is difficult to predict stress patterns in Owa.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: line 107 '=== Stress ===', line 109 carries the three quoted sentences verbatim once wiki templates ({{lang}}, {{IPA}}, {{gloss}}, {{sfn}}) are stripped: 'Usually, the second-to-last syllable is stressed... auragi /ɐʊ.ˈɾɐ.gɪ/ married... occasionally the antepenultimate... fefene /ˈfɛ.fɛ.nɛ/ female... stress placement depends on the context... difficult to predict stress patterns in Owa.' Minor locator nit: only the first two sentences carry {{sfn|Mellow|2013|p=5}}; the third (context/unpredictability) sentence is unfootnoted, so that caveat is the Wikipedia editor's wording with no page cite. Identity: the article's infobox has iso3=stn, glotto=owaa1237, dialects Tawarafa/Owa R…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Default word stress on the penultimate syllable; some words carry antepenultimate stress instead (e.g. fefene 'female'); realised stress also shifts with position in the sentence, so the author (as summarised) treats it as not fully predictable.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing reported in the accessible (second-hand) text.
new_statements.exceptions: Antepenultimate stress in some words (fefene /ˈfɛ.fɛ.nɛ/ 'female'); sentence-position effects on stress placement.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement with an explicit caveat that placement varies with sentence context (phrase-level interaction); examples are citation forms. Second-hand summary only — Mellow's own wording on p. 5 not seen (note: 'penultimate' does not occur in Mellow's text per Google Books index, so his phrasing differs).
new_statements.identity_note: All statements concern Owa [stn] = Glottolog owaa1237 as described by Mellow (dialects Tawarafa, Owa Raha, Owa Riki per Wikipedia summarising Mellow). Owa forms a dialect chain with Kahua [agw] (kahu1239); Mellow's data are from Santa Ana (Owa Raha) / Star Harbour area. No dialect-specific stress differences reported in what was accessible.
